description: Event ingestion requests to the Mixpanel track endpoint, which posts a bare array of events. /import is vendor/mixpanel-import. /engage is vendor/mixpanel-engage. /groups is vendor/mixpanel-groups.

params.name: ip
params.description: Mixpanel documents `ip=1` so the request address is used to compute a `distinct_id` when none is sent.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Mixpanel documents `verbose=1` so the 200 body says whether the track call was accepted.

params.name: img
params.description: Mixpanel documents `img=1` so the response is a 1x1 transparent pixel.

params.name: event
params.description: Mixpanel documents the event name as required.
params.fix_hint: Name the event, such as `Signed Up`.

params.name: properties
params.description: Mixpanel documents the properties object as required, since the project token rides inside it.
params.fix_hint: Add a `properties` object carrying at least `token`.

params.name: properties.token
params.description: It is the project token the event is attributed to.
params.fix_hint: Send the project token from your Mixpanel project settings.

params.name: properties.distinct_id
params.description: It identifies the user who performed the event. Mixpanel documents it as the unique user identifier; without it the event is not tied to a person.
params.fix_hint: Send the same `distinct_id` you use elsewhere for this user.

params.name: properties.time
params.description: Mixpanel documents `time` as a Unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds. A non-numeric value is not that format.
params.fix_hint: Send seconds or milliseconds since epoch, as an integer.

params.name: properties.$insert_id
params.description: Mixpanel uses it to drop duplicates, so a retried request is not counted twice. `/import` requires it in vendor/mixpanel-import.
params.fix_hint: Send a stable id per event.

params.name: properties.ip
params.description: Mixpanel uses `properties.ip` for GeoIP. This is different from the query `ip` flag. Send an address, not a digest.

params.name: properties.$current_url
params.description: It is the URL of the page on which the event was tracked. Mixpanel documents `$current_url` on the JavaScript SDK default-property table.
params.fix_hint: Send an absolute URL in `properties.$current_url`, including the scheme.

params.name: properties.$referrer
params.description: It is the referring URL, including your own domain. Mixpanel documents `$referrer` on the JavaScript SDK default-property table. `$direct` belongs on `$initial_referrer`, not here.
params.fix_hint: Send an absolute referring URL, or omit the field when `document.referrer` is empty.

params.name: properties.mp_lib
params.description: It names the Mixpanel library that sent the event, such as `web`, `android`, `swift`, `react-native`, or `flutter`. Mixpanel documents `mp_lib` on the SDK default-property table.
params.fix_hint: Send `properties.mp_lib`, or drop the empty pair.

params.name: properties.$lib_version
params.description: It is the Mixpanel library version. Mixpanel documents `$lib_version` on the SDK default-property table.
params.fix_hint: Send `properties.$lib_version`, or drop the empty pair.

params.name: properties.$device_id
params.description: It is the device-local Mixpanel ID. Mixpanel documents `$device_id` as regenerated by `reset()`.
params.fix_hint: Send `properties.$device_id`, or drop the empty pair.

params.name: properties.$user_id
params.description: It is the identified user ID. Mixpanel documents `$user_id` as set by `identify()`.
params.fix_hint: Send `properties.$user_id` after identify, or drop the empty pair.

params.name: properties.$screen_height
params.description: It is the device screen height in pixels, or points on iOS. Mixpanel documents `$screen_height` on the SDK default-property table.
params.fix_hint: Send `properties.$screen_height` as an integer pixel or point count.

params.name: properties.$screen_width
params.description: It is the device screen width in pixels, or points on iOS. Mixpanel documents `$screen_width` on the SDK default-property table.
params.fix_hint: Send `properties.$screen_width` as an integer pixel or point count.

rules.message: `properties.ip` looks like a SHA-256 digest, but Mixpanel documents it as an IP address.
